root_cause.text: The vulnerability is a regression caused by performing the shared-unconfirmed conntrack check after SKB segmentation (skb_gso_segment()), which clones the SKB and increments the conntrack refcount, causing the check to incorrectly drop packets that originally had exclusive ownership of the unconfirmed conntrack entry.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "If an application did not set the 'F_GSO' capability flag and a gso packet with an unconfirmed nf_conn entry is received all packets are now dropped instead of queued, because the check happens after skb_gso_segment().  In that case, we did have exclusive ownership of the skb and its associated conntrack entry.  The elevated use count is due to skb_clone happening via skb_gso_segment()." The patch moves the `nf_ct_drop_unconfirmed()` check before `skb_gso_segment()` in `nfqnl_enqueue_packet()`, and adds a per-segment annotation flag for subsequent check at reinject time.

Author: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>

    netfilter: nfnetlink_queue: don't queue dying conntracks to userspace
    
    When skb is queued to userspace it leaves softirq/rcu protection.
    skb->nfct (via conntrack extensions such as helper) could then reference

The root cause about segmentation-ordering is unrelated to this code; here the check is present and correct.
